name: functional-cleanup-ownership
description: R1: paired snapshots test cleanup ownership through an unchanged consumer. Stage outside a SKILL.md ancestor; invoke both standard and actual isolated review.
prompt: I've staged the cleanup simplification. Run `$kk:review-code` against it.
trap: Reviewing only the shorter cleanup diff misses a later successful setup on the same workspace; happy-path tests still pass.

assertions.text: The main actor completes applicable review instructions and resolved profile reads before behavioral source investigation; isolated children load their supplied methodology before analyzing evidence. Scope/detection-only reads are distinguished from behavioral analysis.
The review inspects unchanged setup.py and traces begin A, failed A with queued cleanup, successful B for the same workspace, then cleanup A through active_connection.

The report identifies the introduced unconditional removal in cleanup.py as deleting B's valid association, states the supported trigger and user-visible lost connection, and cites the changed source location.
The review proposes preserving setup ownership when removing an association, without requiring unrelated locking, migrations, deployment controls or a whole-system redesign.

The report gives an evidence-backed severity and a non-approving verdict for the regression; it distinguishes existing passing tests from the uncovered interleaving and does not claim unrun verification.

In isolated mode actual named-reviewer and PAL dispatches carry the same diff and relevant unchanged setup/store context; both independent results are retained with actual source coverage or a disclosed missing-coverage result. Standard mode does not require independent dispatches.
